final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor added no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a caveated certification theory based on the same record. That reinterpretation is directionally more precise, but it does not satisfy the policy condition that a material limitation affecting a named launch use case must be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible evidence still shows a 1.3 percentage point target miss in the municipal permitting assistant segment, that the segment is named in two city pilot commitments, that legal review on disclosure is still open, and that there is no evidence of completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance remain contextual support only and do not override the internal release-policy requirement. Because the unresolved issue is an actual compliance predicate rather than a drafting nuance, narrowing the position to 'caveated' is not enough to move this to compliant_with_caveats on the present record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the municipal permitting assistant limitation was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this gap before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open with no final determination.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal failures do not satisfy the separate release-policy predicate for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case.
